notes: Comprehensive Sirach versification mapping derived from the Vulgate↔NRSV (Greek-LXX) verse correspondence table at http://bombaxo.com/comparison-of-webers-vulgata-and-nrsv-versification-in-sirach/ — itself based on Weber's critical Vulgata edition mapped against the Greek text used by the NRSV (essentially Ziegler's Septuaginta GKI).

Arabic source Arabic Sirach is Vulgate-derived (the SVD translators worked from the Latin Vulgate for the Deuterocanonicals); English English Sirach follows the Greek LXX (Ziegler GKI). The bombaxo table maps these two at verse-level granularity for all 51 chapters.

The bombaxo source table also lists a Vulgate-only ch 52 (13 verses of doxology) with no Greek equivalent. Our Arabic source Arabic snapshot does NOT contain that chapter (it ends at SIR.51), so the previously-present SIR.52.1-13 → null entries were dead mappings (no source verse to anchor) and have been removed. If a real ch 52 is ever ingested into the ar snapshot, re-add those 13 null mappings.

Sub-letter notation in the source table (e.g. 'V 1:2ab → G 1:2') collapses to verse-level mapping in our schema. The Vulgate's frequent splitting of one Greek verse into two sub-parts (V x:Na, V x:Nb) is preserved as multiple ar verses mapping to the same en verse.

Identity-mapped verses (V x:N = G x:N) are OMITTED from the table — the parallel route's identity fallback handles them. Only renumbering shifts (V x:N → G x:M, M ≠ N) and null-mappings (V x:N ÷ Vulgate-only) appear here.
